messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Deducer 0.4-2 and DeducerExtras 1.1 Released
parts:
Deducer 0.4-2 and DeducerExtras 1.2 have been released to CRAN, and
will propagate across the mirrors in due course.

Deducer 0.4-2 contains a few bug fixes, and an interface to the iplots
package. With the new iplots interface it is now possible to do
interactive plots with Deducer. An introductory example screen cast is
up on youtube:

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T6kOvlMaFCA

DeducerExtras 1.2 contains a few new dialogs including 'load data from
package', and 't-test power'.


Additionally, a new Windows R/JGR/Deducer installer is available which
installs R-2.12.0, JGR with it's launcher, Deducer, DeducerExtras, and
DeducerPlugInScaling. It is available on the Deducer website:
http://www.deducer.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php?n=Main.WindowsInstallation

Ian

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Deducer 0.4-2 and DeducerExtras 1.1 Released
parts:
Thanks for the bug report. Your file associations for .bat files are
broken. The install did not complete successfully. It missed the part
where all the R packages are installed, and your java is checked. The
association can be fixed with:

assoc .bat=batfile

The installer now works even if your .bat associations are broken.

Ian

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Deducer 0.4-2 and DeducerExtras 1.1 Released
parts:
I'm glad you made it through okay. Sounds like quite the experience.

The question is not so much a Deducer question, but a statistical one. I'll try to give some guidance anyway. The relationship does not appear to be overtly non-linear, but there does seem to be something special about Myoele and Myokea. If there is something physiologically different about these two bats and Myones does not share this feature, you might try redoing the prediction with Myoele and Myokea excluded. There is a fair degree of variability in the data, so I wouldn't expect that you will be able to get predictions that very closely match the actual frequencies. If you had additional body measurements you might be able to use those to improve your estimates.

Ian
